beats.text: Same hundred thousand dollars of profit. Incorporate, and you keep about six thousand more. But not from lower tax.
Option one: sole proprietor in Manitoba. About twenty-one thousand seven hundred of income tax, plus about ninety-three hundred of CPP. You keep about sixty-nine thousand.
Option two: a corporation that pays it all out as dividends. Nine percent corporate tax, then tax on the dividends. About twenty-five thousand. More income tax, not less.
So where does the six thousand come from? Dividends skip CPP. No contributions, but no CPP pension built, and no RRSP room.
The real edge is money you leave inside. Leave forty thousand in the company, and so far it's only been taxed at nine percent.
A corporation also files its own tax return every year. Run your numbers with an accountant first.
Next: salary or dividends. What should an owner pay themselves? Follow so you don't miss it.
